reason: The membrane fats have water-facing heads and water-avoiding tails, so putting them in water seems like a good way to start the cell’s outer enclosure.
expectation: The fats will arrange in water to form a membrane enclosure.

alternatives.reason: The envelope also looks ready to enclose the DNA, but I’ll start with the outer enclosure.

effect: The fats and water formed the membrane bag, completing the enclosure goal and revealing a goal to add routes for water and sugar.
reaction: The picture makes it satisfying to see how the fats form a wall with water on both sides.
reason: The water-channel protein has a pore for water and appears designed to span the membrane, so it should give the bag a water route.
expectation: The water-channel protein will fit into the membrane bag as a route for water.

alternatives.reason: The envelope appears ready to enclose the DNA, but I can work on the new boundary goal first.

effect: The water channel fitted into the bag, providing a route across its boundary; the sugar route is still needed.
reaction: The arrows make the channel’s job clear.
reason: The sugar-carrier protein spans a membrane and has a sugar-shaped pocket, so it looks like the matching route for sugar.
expectation: The sugar carrier will fit into the membrane alongside the water channel.

alternatives.reason: That looks like a way to work on the nucleus goal instead.

effect: The sugar carrier fitted into the bag, completing the goal of providing routes for water and sugar.
reaction: The picture makes it clear that the carrier opens to both sides of the boundary.
reason: The nuclear envelope surrounds an open space, so it looks ready to enclose the DNA for the remaining goal.
expectation: The DNA will be enclosed by the nuclear envelope to form a nucleus.

effect: The DNA is now enclosed in a nucleus, and the new goal is to put it inside the cell boundary.
reaction: The picture shows that a copy of an instruction can leave through a pore, which is interesting.
reason: The membrane bag is the cell boundary, so fitting the nucleus into it directly addresses the new goal.
expectation: The nucleus will be placed inside the membrane bag.

effect: The nucleus is inside the membrane bag, completing the final goal and the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the cell parts assembled in one enclosure.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the membrane bag was most worthwhile: the picture showed how the fats form a wall with water on both sides, creating an inside and outside.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the two routes felt a little repetitive, though their pictures showed different ways across the boundary.

surprise.text: I was interested that a copy of a DNA instruction could leave the nucleus through a pore while the DNA stayed inside.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals made the pairings clear.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter to see how the cell connects to tissues and organs, though this chapter's pairings were mostly predictable.
